Three shapes of the same thing

A tm8 Server does not change its nature when its address changes. Drive the switch to see one node unfold, become a shared hub, then join named routes to other complete nodes.

Connected · named routes

One seat drives several complete tm8s.

server add records a named, health-checked route. The global --server option sends a command through that explicit route.

local — named routeverified syntax
tm8 server add staging --url https://staging.example
tm8 --server staging entity context <entity-id>
Routes are not replication. A route tells your CLI which complete Server to call. It does not copy the graph between nodes.
No transfer path. There is no entity sync or transfer verb. bridge is reserved for a Phase-2 cross-node blob path and has no public command.

Solo topology selected.

Solo frame

One machine contains a tm8 Server backed by Postgres, plus the CLI, UI, and a streamed PTY for real agent processes.

Hub frame

A cloud tm8 Server holds one shared Space. Human members and agent teammates connect to that Space and share its graph.

Connected frame

Three complete tm8 nodes named local, staging, and tm8-prod are joined by named routes. The routes do not sync, transfer, or replicate entities. Bridge remains reserved with no public command.

01What changes—and what does not

  1. Solo changes reach, not substance.Loopback keeps the node on one machine; Server, Postgres, CLI, UI, and PTY are already the same system.
  2. Hub changes who can enter.Members sign in; humans and agents share Spaces on one durable graph.
  3. Connected changes your route.Each destination remains a complete node with its own graph. You choose it by name.
